recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一個中型母細胞，核圓、染色質細緻、核質比高，最具特徵的是細胞質邊緣有多個凸出的小芽狀突起（cytoplasmic blebs），提示巨核母細胞，符合唐氏症相關骨髓性白血病。
features: Medium-sized blast with high N:C ratio
Round to slightly irregular nucleus with fine, open chromatin
Scant basophilic cytoplasm with small cytoplasmic blebs/protrusions
No cytoplasmic granules or Auer rods evident
Background red cells show mild anisocytosis; platelets appear sparse
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a circulating blast with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, a round to slightly irregular nucleus with fine open chromatin and a scant rim of basophilic cytoplasm bearing small cytoplasmic blebs. Granules and Auer rods are not seen. Platelets appear decreased in this field. The blebbed cytoplasm suggests megakaryoblastic differentiation, and in a child with Down syndrome, findings are consistent with myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome.

ddx.vs: Lymphoblasts lack cytoplasmic blebs and are TdT/CD19 or CD3 positive, whereas megakaryoblasts express CD41/CD61.
TAM blasts are morphologically identical, so age (neonate) and clinical course, not morphology, separate it.
Reactive lymphocytes have more condensed chromatin and abundant cytoplasm that indents around red cells.
Hairy cells have circumferential fine hairy projections, oval or bean-shaped nuclei with bland chromatin and a mature B-cell CD11c/CD25/CD103 phenotype.
